chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever fears an affliction that may befall him, and then precedes it with supplication, God, Mighty and Majestic, will never show him that affliction.

key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Supplication, invocation, prayer to God — the spiritual instrument that wards off affliction
key_terms.بَلَاء: Affliction, trial, tribulation — divine testing that may befall a person
key_terms.تَخَوَّفَ: To be fearful/apprehensive, to anticipate with dread
key_terms.تَقَدَّمَ: To precede, to come before, to be proactive — the key concept of acting in advance

ai.seo_question: Does supplication before an affliction prevent it from occurring in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that proactive supplication — making du'a in anticipation of a feared affliction before it occurs — serves as a divine shield that prevents the affliction from ever materializing. This hadith was transmitted through a chain that includes well-known companions of the Imam, and it addresses the Shia community's understanding of du'a as an active spiritual tool for warding off harm, not merely a passive petition after calamity strikes.
